Papers are read against six fields, in the order below, so entries stay comparable. Each
paper has its own page — the card links through. Terms are collected in the
[Methods Glossary](glossary.qmd); the papers the pipeline itself is built on are cited on
the [Resources](resources.qmd) page.

## How each paper is read

**1. Year published**
: Establishes what was technically possible at the time. A 2010 microarray study and a 2025
deep-proteomics study are not making the same kind of claim.

**2. Model(s) used**
: Which species, whether the comparison is within or across species, and whether the
cross-species claim rests on the same tissue.

**3. Brain region**
: Recorded whenever stated. **Cerebrovascular endothelium differs between brain regions**,
and between arterial, capillary and venous segments of the same vessel tree, so a gene
"BBB-enriched" in one region or segment may not be in another. Where a paper does not state
the region — or where regions are not matched between species — that is recorded too.

**4. What is measured**
: DNA, RNA, or protein. Sequence conservation and expression answer different questions, and
a paper measuring RNA cannot on its own support a claim about conservation.

**5. How it is measured**
: Microarray, bulk RNA-seq, single-cell/nucleus RNA-seq, proteomics, genomic sequencing. For
RNA-seq, **bulk or single-cell**, and whether cells were sorted. Bulk brain tissue drowns
endothelial signal in neurons; isolated microvessels or sorted endothelium do not.

**6. Statistical and modelling techniques**
: What was done to compare across species — orthologue assignment, differential tests and
thresholds, alignment, selection estimates, phylogenetic versus pairwise, multiple-testing
correction.

### [Park et al. 2019](papers/park2019.qmd)

::: {.paper-meta}
[2019]{.pm} [Human only, in vitro]{.pm} [Barrier function]{.pm} [Organ-on-a-chip]{.pm}
:::

A human blood brain barrier built on a two channel microfluidic chip, from iPSC-derived
endothelium differentiated under hypoxia and interfaced with primary human astrocytes and
pericytes. It holds barrier function for a week, shows working efflux pumps rather than
merely present ones, and delivers a clinically approved antibody across the barrier by
reversible osmotic opening. No cross-species comparison at all, which is the point: it is an
attempt to skip the species jump entirely.

[Read the entry →](papers/park2019.qmd)
:::

::: {.paper-card}
### [Kumabe et al. 2025](papers/kumabe2025.qmd)

::: {.paper-meta}
[2025]{.pm} [Human · cynomolgus monkey · mouse]{.pm} [Protein]{.pm} [DIA proteomics]{.pm}
:::

Deep proteomic profiling of brain microvessels isolated from all three species, alongside
five cultured BBB model cell types. Clustering puts human closest to monkey and mouse
furthest out — the same ordering this project finds in coding sequence, reached from protein
expression instead. Also the primate BBB expression data the pipeline currently lacks, and a
clear demonstration that immortalised cell lines drift away from real brain endothelium.

[Read the entry →](papers/kumabe2025.qmd)
:::
